# Bot Registration and Server Lockdown

Covers Developer Portal setup, OAuth2, permissions, and locking a bot to a
private server. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## Bot Creation (Developer Portal)

1. Create application at `https://discord.com/developers/applications` [9]
2. Get Application ID and Public Key from General Information [9]
3. Bot user is "enabled by default" on the Bot settings page [9]
4. Get Bot Token from Bot page (regenerate if needed) [9]
5. Configure privileged intents on Bot settings page [9]
6. Enable Installation Contexts (User Install / Guild Install) [9]
7. Add scopes: `applications.commands` for both contexts, `bot` for guild [9]
8. Select permissions (e.g., Send Messages) [9]
9. Use Install Link to add bot to server [9]

Credentials for `.env` file: Application ID, Public Key, Bot Token [9].

## OAuth2 Scopes and Invite URL

| Scope | Purpose | Source |
|-------|---------|--------|
| `bot` | Places bot user in selected guild | [7] |
| `applications.commands` | Registers slash commands in guild | [7] |

The `applications.commands` scope is "included by default with the bot scope" —
no separate request needed. [7]

### Invite URL Format

```
https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=<ID>&scope=bot&permissions=<INT>
```

| Parameter | Purpose | Source |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `client_id` | Application ID | [7] |
| `scope` | `bot` (includes `applications.commands`) | [7] |
| `permissions` | Bitwise permission integer | [7] |
| `guild_id` | Pre-select target guild (optional) | [7] |
| `disable_guild_select` | Lock to pre-selected guild (optional) | [7] |

Bot authorization does not require `response_type` or `redirect_uri`. [7]

## Permission System

53 permission flags stored as 64-bit integers, combined via bitwise OR. [5]

### Key Permissions for Personal Automation

| Permission | Hex Value | Decimal | Purpose |
|------------|-----------|---------|---------|
| VIEW_CHANNEL | 0x400 | 1024 | See channels | [5] |
| SEND_MESSAGES | 0x800 | 2048 | Post messages | [5] |
| READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY | 0x10000 | 65536 | Read past messages | [5] |
| ADD_REACTIONS | 0x40 | 64 | React to messages | [5] |
| MANAGE_ROLES | 0x10000000 | 268435456 | Modify overwrites | [5] |
| ADMINISTRATOR | 0x8 | 8 | Bypass all overwrites | [5] |

**Minimum viable permission integer** for a personal bot that sends messages and
reads channels: `VIEW_CHANNEL | SEND_MESSAGES` = 0x400 | 0x800 = **3072**.

**Avoid ADMINISTRATOR** — it "bypasses all channel overwrites" and is overprivileged
for personal automation. [5]

## Channel Overwrite Resolution (8 Steps)

1. Base `@everyone` permissions (guild-wide) [5]
2. Role permissions layer in [5]
3. `@everyone` deny overwrites apply [5]
4. `@everyone` allow overwrites apply [5]
5. Role deny overwrites apply [5]
6. Role allow overwrites apply [5]
7. Member deny overwrites apply [5]
8. Member allow overwrites apply [5]

Calculation: remove denied (`&= ~deny`), then add allowed (`|= allow`). [5]

ADMINISTRATOR short-circuits the entire process — grants all permissions. [5]

### Creating a Bot-Only Channel

To isolate a channel to the bot and server owner:

1. Deny `VIEW_CHANNEL` on `@everyone` at channel level (steps 3-4) [5]
2. Allow `VIEW_CHANNEL` and `SEND_MESSAGES` on bot's role or member
   overwrite (steps 5-8) [5]

The server owner has implicit administrator access and can always see the
channel. [5]

## Private Server Lockdown

For a personal automation bot on a private server:

| Setting | Recommendation | Source |
|---------|---------------|--------|
| Public Bot toggle | Off (only owner can invite) | [9] |
| Server members | Owner only | — |
| Bot permissions | Minimum viable (3072 for send+view) | [5] |
| Bot-only channel | @everyone denied VIEW_CHANNEL | [5] |
| Privileged intents | Enable MESSAGE_CONTENT in portal | [1] |

Unverified bots (under 75 guilds) can enable privileged intents without
approval — just toggle in the Developer Portal. [1]

## Role Hierarchy Constraints

- Bots grant roles only below their highest role position [5]
- Bots edit roles below their own highest position [5]
- Users with higher role position cannot be kicked/banned by the bot [5]
- ADMINISTRATOR overrides all hierarchy constraints [5]
